A Sunday on La Grande Jatte

Georges Seurat, 1884–1886

Oil on canvas

Riverside park scene built from small dots of pure colour.

Use this style

Georges Seurat, A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, 1884–1886. Art Institute of Chicago. Source on Wikimedia Commons. Licence: Public domain.

About the painting

Seurat spent two years on this view of Parisians relaxing on an island in the Seine. Instead of mixing colours on the palette, he placed small dots and dashes of separate colours side by side and let the viewer's eye mix them, a method later called pointillism. The canvas is about two by three metres.

It was the centrepiece of the eighth and last Impressionist exhibition in 1886, and it launched Neo-Impressionism. The painted border of dots was added a few years later. The Art Institute of Chicago has owned it since 1926.

How it looks on your photo

A quiet style. Photos shift towards deep greens and sunlit yellow and gain a fine, grainy texture rather than large visible dots. It keeps detail well, so it works on almost anything, especially parks, water and people outdoors.
